column1: # TH8 system-dependency manifest -- the single source of truth for the
# `make pkg-deps-core|pkg-deps-static|pkg-deps-test` targets (and their
# deprecated apt-deps* aliases).  Read by tools/pkgdeps.sh.
# Format: TAB-separated, exactly three fields:
#     <feature>  <manager>  <space-separated package list>
#   feature : core | static | test
#               core   = everything needed for a standard dynamic build
#               static = the extra -dev libs a fully-static link needs
#               test   = the dynamic-analysis toolchain (valgrind, sanitizers)
#   manager : apt (Debian/Ubuntu) | brew (macOS/Homebrew)
# A `<feature>  note-<manager>  <text>` row carries a caveat printed before
# install (e.g. packages that map to something other than a manager package).
# Lines beginning with `#` are comments.  Keep the package lists on ONE line.
# clang-format-19 tracks CLANG_FORMAT_VERSION in the Makefile; update both if
# the pinned version changes.
# Why TH8 needs each package (apt name / brew name -- purpose):
# core -- required to build TH8 (`make all`):
#   build-essential / (Xcode CLT)   gcc + make + libc/pthread/dl headers: the
#                                   compiler toolchain.  On macOS this is the
#                                   Xcode Command Line Tools, not a brew formula.
#   pkg-config / pkg-config         resolves OpenSSL and unbound compile/link
#                                   flags at build time (libcurl via curl-config).
#   tcl-dev / tcl-tk@8              tclsh 8.6: runs ALL build tooling -- genstubs,
#                                   the `vendoring` generators, mkreq, check_*,
#                                   and the Tcl/Eagle test harness -- and supplies
#                                   the Tcl stubs the [th8] Tcl bridge and the
#                                   test library link against.
#   clang-format-19 / (pip venv)   the canonical formatter the `audit-format`
#                                   gate enforces (pinned major version; see
#                                   CLANG_FORMAT_VERSION).  No brew formula pins
#                                   19, so macOS uses a pinned pip venv instead.
#   mandoc / mandoc                the man-page linter `make manlint` (part of
#                                   `make all`); without it manlint skips rather
#                                   than fails, but CI installs it to lint.
#   libssl-dev / openssl@3         OpenSSL: signed-script / certificate crypto
#                                   (TH8_ENABLE_CRYPTOGRAPHY, the signed-only
#                                   policy, RSA/hashing).
#   libcurl4-openssl-dev / (SDK)   libcurl: HTTPS transport for `clock https`,
#                                   remote signed [load], and [source <url>]
#                                   (TH8_ENABLE_LIBCURL).  macOS ships libcurl in
#                                   the SDK -- no brew pkg (the build links -lcurl).
#   libunbound-dev / unbound       libunbound: the DNSSEC-validating resolver
#                                   (TH8_ENABLE_UNBOUND).  Omit it and build
#                                   `make ENABLE_UNBOUND=0` to drop DNS support.
# static -- LINUX ONLY: the extra -dev packages a FULLY-STATIC libcurl link needs
# (STATIC_ENABLE_LIBCURL=1).  Dynamic builds need NONE of this.  macOS statically
# links nothing (Apple ships no static libSystem), so no brew names.  Every
# archive below was verified PRESENT on Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) amd64 via
# packages.ubuntu.com (searchon=contents) on 2026-08-07.  libcurl.a itself and
# libssl.a/libcrypto.a come from the 'core' row (libcurl4-openssl-dev, libssl-dev)
# and are NOT repeated here.
#   package (apt)     static archive(s) it ships       why the static link needs it
#   zlib1g-dev        libz.a                           curl: transfer compression
#   libnghttp2-dev    libnghttp2.a                     curl: HTTP/2
#   libbrotli-dev     libbrotlidec.a libbrotlicommon.a curl: brotli content-encoding
#   libzstd-dev       libzstd.a                        curl: zstd content-encoding
#   libidn2-dev       libidn2.a                        curl: internationalized domains
#   libunistring-dev  libunistring.a                   REQUIRED by libidn2.a
#   libpsl-dev        libpsl.a                         curl: public-suffix cookie policy
#   libssh-dev        libssh.a                         curl: SFTP/SCP protocol handler
#   librtmp-dev       librtmp.a                        curl: RTMP protocol handler
#   libldap-dev       libldap.a liblber.a              curl: LDAP protocol handler
#   libsasl2-dev      libsasl2.a                       curl/ldap: SASL auth
# NOTE: on noble the real package is `libldap-dev`; `libldap2-dev` is now just a
# transitional wrapper for it.
# DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED:
#   * MIT krb5 / GSS-API: `libkrb5-dev` ships NO `.a` on ANY Ubuntu release
#     (noble AND jammy both verified) -- only Heimdal (heimdal-multidev) has a
#     libkrb5.a, and at a non-default path.  A static libcurl link succeeds
#     without it: TH8's HTTPS-only use never pulls curl's Negotiate/GSS-API
#     objects, so `-lgssapi_krb5` is never demanded.  (Confirmed empirically --
#     the same static link works on a stock 22.04 box, which ALSO lacks the
#     archive; this is why the earlier "24.04 dropped static libs" theory was
#     wrong.  The real 24.04 failure was simply un-installed -dev packages.)
#   * The unbound static chain (libevent-dev; nettle-dev = libnettle.a +
#     libhogweed.a; libgmp-dev; libunbound.a lives in the core libunbound-dev)
#     is omitted because STATIC_BUILD defaults ENABLE_UNBOUND=0.  A static build
#     WITH unbound additionally needs those three -- all verified present on noble.
# If a static link ever reports "attempted static link of dynamic object", the
# named archive's -dev package is absent from the row below; the static-shell CI
# job's "Diagnose static libs" step prints exactly which `.a` the runner has.
# test -- the dynamic-analysis toolchain (NOT needed for a normal build):
#   valgrind / (n/a)               `make valgrind` memcheck, plus the Valgrind
#                                   headers that mimalloc's MI_TRACK_VALGRIND
#                                   annotations compile against.  Linux only --
#                                   valgrind is unavailable on macOS/Apple Silicon.
#   clang / (n/a)                  Linux: `make msan` (MemorySanitizer is
#                                   clang-only; gcc cannot do it) and libFuzzer
#                                   (FUZZ_CC defaults to clang).  macOS installs
#                                   nothing -- the system Apple clang (Xcode CLT,
#                                   from 'core') already provides clang and the
#                                   asan/ubsan sanitizers; MSan is unavailable.
#                                   `make asan` / `ubsan` / `sanitize` need NO
#                                   extra package on either OS (gcc/Apple clang
#                                   ship the sanitizer runtimes).
#   llvm / (n/a)                   Linux: llvm-cov + llvm-profdata for the
#                                   `make mcdc` MC/DC coverage report (needs
#                                   clang >= 18 for -fmcdc-coverage; the default
#                                   clang on the CI's ubuntu-latest is 18).
#                                   macOS uses xcrun's llvm-* -- nothing to add.
# fuzz -- the fuzzing toolchain (Linux CI only; NOT for a normal build):
#   afl++ / (n/a)                  afl-clang-fast for the AFL++ campaign
#                                   (`make afl`).  libFuzzer's smoke pass uses
#                                   clang (from `test`/system), not afl++.
core
column3: build-essential pkg-config tcl-dev clang-format-19 mandoc libssl-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev libunbound-dev

column3: build-essential -> Xcode Command Line Tools (run: xcode-select --install); clang-format-19 -> pinned pip venv, provisioned automatically (see docs/public/portability.md); libcurl and zlib are provided by the macOS SDK (no brew package)

column1: static
column3: nothing to install: TH8 does not statically link on macOS (Apple ships no static libSystem); the fully-static libs are a Linux-only concern

column1: test
test
column3: nothing to install: the sanitizers (asan/ubsan) use the system Apple clang from the Xcode CLT (installed by 'core'); valgrind, MemorySanitizer, and the llvm-cov/-profdata MC/DC tooling are unavailable on macOS

fuzz
column3: nothing to install: libFuzzer uses the system Apple clang; AFL++ (afl-clang-fast) is not provided here
